Use induction to prove that $4^n+14$ is divisible by 6 for all positive integers $n$.
questions.answer:
$n=1$: $18=6\times3$.

Assume $4^k+14=6M$. Then $4^{k+1}+14=4(6M-14)+14=24M-42=6(4M-7)$, divisible by 6.

Hence true for all $n\ge1$ by induction.

A projectile is fired from $O$ with speed $V$ m/s at angle of elevation $\theta$, with constant downward acceleration $g\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ (see diagram). Find the horizontal and vertical displacements after $t$ seconds.
questions.answer:
$\ddot x=0$, $\ddot y=-g$. Integrating with $\dot x(0)=V\cos\theta$, $\dot y(0)=V\sin\theta$:

$x=Vt\cos\theta$, $y=Vt\sin\theta-\frac12gt^2$.

questions.answer:
$[\ln(\sec x+\tan x)]_0^1=\ln(\sec1+\tan1)\approx\ln3.408=1.23$ (radians).

Part of the curve $y=1+\cos2x$ is shown; it meets $y=1$ at $x=a$ and $x=b$. The region between the curve and $y=1$ from $a=-\frac\pi4$ to $b=\frac\pi4$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the exact volume.

A bowl's interior is formed by rotating $y=\dfrac{x^2}4$ about the $y$-axis (units cm). Water is poured in at $36\ \text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$. When the depth is $h$ cm, the water surface has area $S\ \text{cm}^2$. Find the rate of increase of $h$ when $S=12$.
questions.answer: $V=\pi\int_0^h4y\,dy=2\pi h^2$ and $S=4\pi h$. $\dfrac{dV}{dh}=4\pi h=S=12$, so $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{36}{12}=3$ cm/s.
